# Research Note: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. (BRK-B)
**Date: May 2026**

---

## Snapshot

**Berkshire Hathaway Inc. (BRK-B)** is a diversified financial services and holding company trading at **$473.01 USD** [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]. The company has a market capitalization of **$1.02 trillion** and trades at a P/E ratio of **15.24** [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]. The 52-week range is **$455.19 to $521.26** [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance].

Over the past month, BRK-B has declined **-0.91%**, significantly outperforming the broader market during a period of volatility [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]. This marks Greg Abel's first quarter as CEO following Warren Buffett's transition.

**Macro Context:** The Federal Funds Rate stands at **3.64%** and is falling, while inflation (CPI) continues rising at **330.293** [Source: FRED]. The unemployment rate has risen to **4.3%** [Source: FRED]. The 10Y-2Y Treasury spread is **0.51 bps** and falling [Source: FRED], while the S&P 500 is at **7,230.12** but has declined approximately **11% year-to-date in 2026** [Source: https://www.techi.com/warren-buffett-cash-strategy-berkshire-hathaway/]. This environment favors defensive positioning and cash preservation.

---

## Bull Case

**1. Record Cash Position Provides Massive Optionality**  
Berkshire's cash pile reached a record **$397 billion** in Q1 2026, up from $373 billion at year-end 2025 [Source: https://www.cnn.com/2026/05/02/business/berkshire-hathaway-earnings-buffett]. This represents approximately 39% of market capitalization and provides unprecedented firepower for acquisitions or stock purchases during market dislocations. With the S&P 500 down 11% year-to-date, Berkshire's cash appreciates in relative terms as other assets decline [Source: https://www.techi.com/warren-buffett-cash-strategy-berkshire-hathaway/].

**2. Strong Q1 2026 Operating Performance**  
Operating earnings rose **17.7%** to **$11.35 billion** in Q1 2026 from $9.64 billion in Q1 2025 [Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/berkshire-hathaway-inc-first-quarter-120000566.html]. Net income attributable to shareholders more than doubled to **$10.1 billion** from $4.6 billion year-over-year [Source: https://www.cnn.com/2026/05/02/business/berkshire-hathaway-earnings-buffett]. This demonstrates the fundamental strength of Berkshire's diversified operating businesses independent of equity market volatility.

**3. Insurance Underwriting Remains Profitable**  
Insurance underwriting earnings rose **29%** to **$1.717 billion** in Q1 2026 [Source: https://www.reinsurancene.ws/berkshire-hathaway-reinsurance-underwriting-earnings-rise-29-to-1-717bn-in-q1-2026/]. The critical insurance float grew to **$176.9 billion**, up $0.5 billion from year-end 2025 [Source: https://www.reinsurancene.ws/berkshire-hathaway-reinsurance-underwriting-earnings-rise-29-to-1-717bn-in-q1-2026/], providing low-cost capital for investments.

**4. Massive Market Outperformance in 2026**  
Berkshire has gained approximately **12%** in 2026 versus an **11% loss** for the S&P 500, creating a **23 percentage point spread** [Source: https://www.techi.com/warren-buffett-cash-strategy-berkshire-hathaway/]. For a company of Berkshire's scale ($1.02 trillion market cap), this represents extraordinary relative performance and validates the defensive positioning strategy.

**5. Technology Transformation Underway**  
CEO Greg Abel outlined at the 2026 annual meeting that Berkshire is transitioning from being a "buyer of technology to a builder of technology solutions" and implementing narrow AI to improve productivity and decision-making across subsidiaries [Source: https://www.forbes.com/sites/bill_stone/2026/05/03/berkshire-hathaway-annual-meeting-2026-key-takeaways/]. This modernization could unlock significant operational efficiencies across the conglomerate's diverse businesses.

---

## Bear Case

**1. BNSF Railroad Continues to Underperform**  
BNSF ranked **fifth out of six Class I railroads** in operating margin profitability, though it has improved to fourth place recently [Source: https://www.forbes.com/sites/bill_stone/2026/05/03/berkshire-hathaway-annual-meeting-2026-key-takeaways/]. Despite improving operating margins to **34.5%** in 2025 from 32.0% in 2024, CEO Abel stated "more progress is needed to translate operational improvements into stronger financial results" [Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/berkshire-ceo-bnsf-needs-improve-185026426.html]. BNSF remains "only modestly above its five-year average" [Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/berkshire-ceo-bnsf-needs-improve-185026426.html].

**2. GEICO Facing Higher Auto Claims**  
Berkshire's GEICO auto insurance business "suffered from higher claims in the first quarter" [Source: https://www.reinsurancene.ws/berkshire-hathaway-reinsurance-underwriting-earnings-rise-29-to-1-717bn-in-q1-2026/]. Rising auto claims frequency and severity in an inflationary environment pose ongoing margin pressure for one of Berkshire's largest subsidiaries.

**3. Investment Income Declining Due to Lower Rates**  
Net insurance investment income fell to **$2.26 billion** in Q1 2026 from **$2.519 billion** a year earlier, with Berkshire citing "lower interest rates" as the cause [Source: https://www.reinsurancene.ws/berkshire-hathaway-reinsurance-underwriting-earnings-rise-29-to-1-717bn-in-q1-2026/]. With the Fed Funds rate falling to 3.64% [Source: FRED], this headwind will likely persist.

**4. Leadership Transition Risk**  
May 2026 marked Greg Abel's first annual meeting as CEO without Warren Buffett. While Abel received a "B-Plus" grade from analysts [Source: https://www.barrons.com/articles/berkshire-hathaway-greg-abel-ceo-annual-meeting-performance-181ad9cd], concerns remain about whether he can replicate Buffett's capital allocation track record. Recent articles highlight uncertainty about the event's future and Abel's ability to fill Buffett's shoes [Source: https://www.businessinsider.com/omaha-trip-warren-buffett-berkshire-shareholder-meeting-weekend-abel-future-2026-5].

**5. Conglomerate Discount and Scale Challenges**  
Recent analysis suggests Berkshire's "conglomerate structure makes future capital appreciation problematic" [Source: https://seekingalpha.com/article/4897886-berkshire-hathaway-stock-conglomerate-structure-makes-future-capital-appreciation-problematic]. At over $1 trillion market cap, finding needle-moving acquisition opportunities becomes increasingly difficult, and the massive cash pile earning relatively low returns (even in T-Bills) creates a drag on ROE.

---

## Recent Catalysts

**1. Greg Abel's First Annual Meeting (May 2-3, 2026)**  
The 2026 Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting marked the first without Warren Buffett as CEO. Abel received generally positive reviews, earning a "solid scorecard" from shareholders [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/03/berkshire-ceo-greg-abel-earns-solid-first-scorecard-after-first-annual-meeting.html]. Abel provided quantitative performance metrics and outlined technology transformation initiatives [Source: https://www.forbes.com/sites/bill_stone/2026/05/03/berkshire-hathaway-annual-meeting-2026-key-takeaways/].

**2. Q1 2026 Earnings Release (May 2, 2026)**  
Berkshire reported Q1 operating earnings of **$11.35 billion**, up 17.7% year-over-year but slightly below analyst estimates of $11.56 billion [Source: https://www.cnn.com/2026/05/02/business/berkshire-hathaway-earnings-buffett]. The cash pile hit a record $397 billion [Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jP6EKe6O_k8].

**3. 10-K Filing for FY 2025 (March 2, 2026)**  
Berkshire filed its annual 10-K report for fiscal year ending December 31, 2025 [Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1067983/000119312526083899/brka-20251231.htm], providing comprehensive financial disclosures under Abel's first year as CEO.

**4. BNSF Capital Investment Announcement (January 2026)**  
BNSF announced a **$3.6 billion capital investment plan** for 2026 to support network service performance and asset productivity initiatives [Source: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260126684425/en/BNSF-Announces-%243.6-Billion-Capital-Investment-Plan-for-2026].

## Risks

**Macro Risks:**
- **Earnings recession concerns**: With unemployment rising to 4.3% and CPI continuing to rise [Source: FRED], stagflation risks are increasing. This could pressure consumer-facing businesses like GEICO, utilities, and retail operations.
- **Declining interest rates**: Fed Funds falling to 3.64% [Source: FRED] reduces investment income from Berkshire's massive cash and fixed-income portfolio, as evidenced by the decline in insurance investment income [Source: https://www.reinsurancene.ws/berkshire-hathaway-reinsurance-underwriting-earnings-rise-29-to-1-717bn-in-q1-2026/].
- **Yield curve flattening**: The 10Y-2Y spread at just 0.51 bps and falling [Source: FRED] suggests weakening growth expectations that could impact railroad volumes and manufacturing businesses.

**Company-Specific Risks:**
- **CEO succession execution risk**: Greg Abel's ability to match Buffett's capital allocation track record remains unproven. The market is watching closely for his first major acquisition decision with $397 billion in cash.
- **BNSF profitability drag**: The railroad's fifth-place ranking in operating margins among peers [Source: https://www.forbes.com/sites/bill_stone/2026/05/03/berkshire-hathaway-annual-meeting-2026-key-takeaways/] represents a significant underperforming asset in the portfolio.
- **Auto insurance claims inflation**: GEICO's higher claims in Q1 [Source: https://www.reinsurancene.ws/berkshire-hathaway-reinsurance-underwriting-earnings-rise-29-to-1-717bn-in-q1-2026/] could persist if accident severity continues rising.
- **Opportunity cost of cash**: With nearly 40% of market cap in cash earning modest returns, extended market weakness without deployment opportunities would create meaningful drag on shareholder returns.
- **Equity portfolio concentration**: Despite trimming, concentrated positions in Apple ($60 billion remaining after significant sales) [Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/warren-buffett-sends-wall-street-112000087.html] create mark-to-market volatility risk.

---

## What to Watch Next

**1. Next Earnings Date: August 1, 2026**  
Q2 2026 earnings [Source: Financial Modeling Prep] will be critical for assessing: (a) whether GEICO's claims trends stabilize, (b) BNSF's margin improvement trajectory, (c) any deployment of the record cash pile, and (d) Abel's commentary on capital allocation priorities.

**2. Capital Deployment Decisions**  
With $397 billion in cash [Source: https://www.cnn.com/2026/05/02/business/berkshire-hathaway-earnings-buffett] and the S&P 500 down 11% year-to-date [Source: https://www.techi.com/warren-buffett-cash-strategy-berkshire-hathaway/], the market will scrutinize whether Abel initiates major share buybacks, pursues acquisitions, or increases equity positions. This will define his reputation as a capital allocator.

**3. BNSF Operating Margin Progress**  
Monitor quarterly progress toward BNSF improving from fourth to higher rankings among Class I railroads. Abel has committed to quantitative targets [Source: https://www.forbes.com/sites/bill_stone/2026/05/03/berkshire-hathaway-annual-meeting-2026-key-takeaways/], making this a measurable accountability metric for the new CEO's operational improvement capabilities.
